column2: Vance Weston and Halo Spear (later Tarrant) meet for the first time at the Willows, an old house built in the style known as Hudson River Bracketed. The novel follows their lives before, and especially after, this meeting, sometimes unfolding separately and often together.

In Short History of Christian Missions from Abraham and Paul to Carey, Livingstone, and Duff , George Smith recounts the history of missions beginning with God's heart for the nations as seen in His interactions with Abraham. Honoré de Balzac (1799-1850) fue uno de los grandes maestros de la literatura universal y uno de los principales representantes del realismo francés junto a Flaubert, Zola, Stendhal y Maupassant, entre otros. Poseía una extraordinaria capacidad para observar y retratar la sociedad de su tiempo, convirtiendo sus novelas en un inmenso retrato de la condición humana.

The Emigrants is a family saga of Norwegian farmers who settle in North Dakota in the late 1800s. The author paints a loving portrait of a large cast of characters, all different but hoping to make a better life in America.

History of the Great American Fortunes by Gustavus Myers is a landmark early-20th-century critique of how immense wealth was accumulated in the United States. First published in three volumes between 1909 and 1910, the book examines the rise of powerful American fortunes—from colonial landowners to railroad magnates and industrial monopolists such as the Astors, Vanderbilts, Goulds, Morgans, and Rockefellers.

The Castaways of Disappointment Island is the true story of Charles Eyre, who in 1907 was working as apprentice sailor on the Dundonald, a British four-masted steel barque. Caught in a storm, the Dundonald sank after hitting the rocky coastline of a tiny subantarctic island known as Disappointment Island which lies 500 km below New Zealand.

A descendant of New England witches, Boston socialite Martha Klemm finds herself drawn to the occult. She hypothesizes that while there is evil in this world its presence is as natural as good and it cannot be absolute.

The author of this gothic tale was one of the first Union soldiers to lose his life in the Civil War. His semi-autobiographical novel focuses on a young traveler, Robert Byng, who, returning to New York from many years abroad, occupies an absent friend’s flat.

Joan Raushenbush delivers us with is a lively, accessible introduction to the peoples and cultures of Latin America in the 1930s, written to spark curiosity and respect in young readers. She highlights the region’s diversity—from bustling modern cities to Indigenous traditions that shape daily life—while emphasizing the shared challenges and aspirations that connect Latin American nations.

Hamilton begins with an exploration of the mind-spirit duality of human nature, and its contrasting manifestations in the cultures of the East and West.
